text:
What does Google look for when it ranks local businesses on the map?

Google says three things:

Relevance. Do you match what they searched?
Distance. How close are you?
Prominence. How well known and well reviewed are you?

You can't pay Google for a better spot. You earn it.

A ranking guarantee is like a Hillarys fishing charter guaranteeing you a dhufish.

Lovely thing to hear on the jetty.

Nobody on that boat controls the fish.

And nobody outside Google controls Google.

Easiest ranking win most tradies skip:

Fill in every part of your Google Business Profile.

Right category. Every service. Service areas. Hours. Photos of real jobs.

Google says complete, accurate info helps it match you to the right searches.

Worth checking this week.

Fake reviews. Junk links. Hundreds of copy-paste suburb pages.

Shortcuts like these might work for a month.

Then Google catches up, and you're the one cleaning up the mess.

If someone pitches you a quick win on Google, ask what happens in month two.

A plumber in Midland paid an SEO company for a year. Page one in 90 days, they said.

He never got there. Then he found out he was locked in for 12 months.

If the work is good, you'll stay anyway. If it's no good, you should be free to stop.

https://gimsresults.com.au/post/seo-company-perth-what-to-watch-out-for

Got a call from someone with a "special relationship" with Google? Or offering "priority submit"?

Google's own guide on hiring an SEO warns about both.

Nobody gets a back door into Google.

I'd let that one go to voicemail.
